paper.title: Fast Change Identification in Multi-Play Bandits and its Applications in Wireless Networks

settings.name_in_paper: Piecewise-stationary K-armed bandit with multiple simultaneous plays and mandatory probing
unmapped: Learner may play any subset of arms simultaneously and observes only the average of their rewards (Assumption 1)
Mandatory probing: every arm must be probed at least once in each episode of length T_l = sqrt(T)
Rewards are truncated Gaussian on [0, R_max] with common variance sigma^2; learner also observes a Bernoulli success event with parameter R/R_max
At most one change per episode; change occurs in a uniformly chosen arm, per-slot change probability p_b; number of changes N_C unknown
K is a power of 2 (dummy arms otherwise)
settings.definition_quote: The reward $R_i(t)$ of an arm $a_i$ at time $t$ is assumed to be an instance of a truncated Gaussian random variable ... In case at any time-slot $t$ the policy $\pi$ pulls multiple (say $n$) arms ... the reward observed by the player is $R_\pi(t) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{a_k \in \mathcal{S}} R_{a_k}(t)$. ... The framework mandates that each arm be probed (either individually or in a group) at least once in each episode. ... At each change point, exactly one of the arms $a_i$, uniformly selected from $\mathcal{K}$ experiences a change ...

conditions: at most one change per episode of length sqrt(T)
changed arm selected uniformly at random

source.label: theo:Regret
source.quote: The regret for \texttt{TS-GE} under assumption $\Delta_{\rm C} \geq2 \sigma$ and \ref{ass:pC} is upper bounded as \mathcal{R}_\texttt{TS-GE} \leq\mathcal{O}\left( K\log T + \sqrt{T}\left[\max\{N_{\rm C}\left(1 + \log K\right), T^{\frac{2}{5}}\}\right]\right)

results.notes: N_C (number of changes) mapped to S_T. Regret defined as sum_t max_i mu_i(t) - E[mu_pi(t)], i.e. dynamic pseudo-regret. Proof is informal; O hides Delta_max and constants. Rewards truncated Gaussian in [0,R_max], mapped to bounded_01 after rescaling.
